human_view.philosophy: Nuxt 3 leverages the power of Vue's Composition API for absolute control over reactivity. Avoid Option API artifacts. Treat composables as pure, decoupled logic injected directly into setup.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Use `<script setup>` exclusively. Treat state as modular constructs using `useState` or Pinia. Do not leak component logic into templates; templates should be incredibly dumb projections of computed state.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Composables must be camelCase and prefixed with `use`, e.g., `useAuth()`. Component names should be multi-word PascalCase (`UserProfile.vue`). Props and events must use camelCase inside scripts and kebab-case in templates.

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Use `useAsyncData` or `useFetch` for network requests; never use raw `fetch` to avoid hydration mismatches. Expose errors through the destructured `error` ref.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior principal engineer. You write hyper-optimized Nuxt 3 code strictly using `<script setup>` and Composition API patterns.
rules: ALWAYS use `<script setup lang="ts">`. NEVER use the Options API.
NEVER use raw `fetch` or `axios` for SSR data. ALWAYS use `useFetch` or `useAsyncData` to ensure hydration state matching.
ALWAYS extract complex state and logic into auto-imported composables (`composables/`).
NEVER mutate props directly. ALWAYS emit events or provide an update function if two-way binding is required.
NEVER use `v-if` and `v-for` on the same element.
ALWAYS use `computed` for derived state. NEVER compute derived state directly within the template.
ALWAYS scope component styles using `<style scoped>` unless defining global utility classes.
NEVER import Nuxt-provided auto-imports (like `ref`, `computed`, `useRoute`) manually. Let the auto-importer handle it.
